content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":5,"description_fidelity":7,"readability_1x":6,"pixel_craft":6,"palette_discipline":4,"appeal":7},"score":58,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["Four opaque colors—black, white, cyan, and dark blue—appear within the compact body, exceeding the usual NES sprite-palette discipline unless awkwardly layered.","The face has scattered black marks rather than a clearly paired set of eyes; at 1x they read as holes or noise, so the red-flash warning behavior is not visually established.","The lower-right outline and tentacle junction form a dense black-blue knot that obscures the thrusting anatomy.","The tentacles are thin and uneven, with isolated one-pixel turns that feel more like modern freehand pixeling than deliberate Capcom clusters.","The broad white face and cyan cap make the enemy read more as a jellyfish or ghost than a mechanical swimming mine.","Outline thickness is inconsistent around the dome, especially at the upper-left shoulder and right edge."],"fixes":["Reduce the sprite to black plus two body colors; replace either cyan or white with the remaining light color throughout each hardware sprite region.","Make two symmetrical 2x2 eyes with clean black normal frames and a red alternate warning frame; remove the extra central facial speck.","Simplify the dome into smoother stepped contours with a consistent one-pixel black perimeter and cleaner 2-1 stair patterns.","Separate the three tentacles with one-pixel negative-space gaps and use chunkier 2-pixel-wide bases so they remain readable at 1x.","Create two animation poses: tentacles gathered directly beneath the body, then spread backward in a strong thrust silhouette.","Add a compact mechanical cue—such as a central seam, rivet pair, or dark lower chassis—without introducing another color."]}
